cards.heading: Definition
cards.question: What is independent fix verification, and what tool envelope does the verifying agent operate under?
cards.answer: A verification loop closed by an agent that took no part in producing the fix; it reads the repo and the finding report under an envelope excluding command execution, network access and writes, then emits a per-finding verdict.

cards.heading: Why separate identity matters
cards.question: Why can't the agent that wrote a fix also be the one that verifies it?
cards.answer: It has already concluded the fix is correct, so asking it to verify would just replay the reasoning that produced the fix — a separate verifier has to re-derive the judgement from artifacts alone.

cards.heading: Why the restricted envelope matters
cards.question: Why is the read-only envelope essential to the verifier's credibility, not just a safety measure?
cards.answer: With no shell it can't make a test pass by re-running or adjusting the harness, with no write access it can't repair the code it's grading, and with no network it can't be steered by fetched content — read-only is what makes the verdict mean something.

cards.heading: Per-finding granularity
cards.question: Why does the verifier emit a verdict per finding rather than one pass/fail over a whole batch?
cards.answer: So partial remediation stays legible instead of collapsing into a single misleading result.

cards.heading: The durable artifact
cards.question: What artifact from the surrounding remediation discipline outlives the agent session and keeps a fixed defect from returning?
cards.answer: The failing-then-passing security test — demonstrate the exploit, turn it into a failing test, fix until it passes, confirm no regressions.
